About The Project:
## Inspiration

We wanted to try and increase student productivity by giving them the ability to create a scheduler that will allocate their time, and hopefully take them out of doomscrolling by giving them a sense of how much time is left. (Sense of dread)

## What it does

A user(student) will give the study planner some inputs to help the scheduler plan out time. Firstly you'll set up the hours and days you're available/want to study (there are default values). You will then add tasks with deadlines and in this view you'll be prompted on an estimate of how many hours you think it will take. Optionally other commitments can be added to the scheduler (work, hobbies, etc.). When that is put in the user will be able to generate a plan within the given time frames and allocate work blocks. If a task cannot fit within a time frame the scheduler will alert the user.

We decided to create a fullstack web app with a backend and frontend communicating. We used the django rest framework for api functions which the frontend calls. And in the frontend we decided to use typescript, react and css to display to users. We used Claude as well to assist in roadmapping the project, as well as creating scaffolding and assisting in writing some logic code in the backend and designing the frontend based off our planned ui.

## Challenges we ran into

A challenge we ran in to was staying within scope and not letting the project get too big for the timeframe. Honestly even with us trying to reel it in the scope got quite big which prompted further use of ai to help with productivity.

## Accomplishments that we're proud of

We are proud to present the project that we have built, we took a decent chunk of time to really lay the ground work for what we wanted the project to be. We're also quite proud of how well our team worked together to get it done on time.

We learned that a project can really get out of hand if we don't define a scope and stick to it. We learned how to implement an algorithm and use ai to assist in production.

About The Project:
## Inspiration

ETS, we talked to you we heard your sufferings and we’ve come to offer an update. the data we received indicated many of the ETS transit users use google maps or Transit app for access and routing. For a truly efficient system the Edmonton Transit system must be robust enough to handle its own population. This would allow proper communication throughout the whole system. We propose a public application that incorporates bus meta data including GPS, bus schedules, proper feedback loop, weather, traffic, &construction. Further more we have proposed a plan for Edmonton and ETS with updates to their hardware for a more robust and seamless user experience.

## What it does

The application pulls data from multiple API's and compiles them to rate and present possible public transit routes to the user. As with other apps, users are able to enter their starting end ending location and are presented with a list of routes. However, our application takes into account often neglected information, such as the possibility of transfer misalignments causing delays in the user's journey.

## How we built it

Our application is built in React. We made extensive use of AI for both the planning and execution of the project. Members of the team brainstormed requirements and researched possible solutions, then worked with AI to generate a project and build plan. From there we used sub-agents to write the code for each feature. We then reviewed functionality and went back to AI tooling to make revisions.

## Challenges we ran into

Our biggest challenge was Anthropic token limits and controlling AI outputs.

## Accomplishments that we're proud of

We are proud of developing such a feature-rich product within a narrow time span.

## What we learned

We learned a lot about the Edmonton Transit system, the applications that have been built to support it, as well as the limitations and process of working through a complex project with an AI-first approach.

## What's next for ETS-Squared

We hope to continue developing and refining the project. In the future we may develop it into a viable alternative to the official ETS app.

About The Project:
## Inspiration

We have been interested in obscure game consoles for a while. And the V.Flash was one of the most interesting: A 3D educational kids console that was like a supercharged version of the PS1. We knew we wanted to see how it operated and how capable it was. We wanted people to be able to develop their own games for the system as we feel like it's a more approachable PS1-like environment to work with; having more modern features while having similar graphics abilities to 5th generation consoles.

## What it does

We have created a unofficial SDK for the V.Flash, allowing curious individuals to make their own games for the console. We have also0 ported Super Mario 64 as a demo proof of concept program to show off what the SDK is capable of.

## How we built it

AI-assisted coding was heavy used, we used Codex with GPT 6.1 Sol; I don’t think it would have been possible in the amount of time provided otherwise. Everything was first ran on an emulator, before being tested on a real console. Open source projects like GCC are used in the SDK to compile to ARMv5 machine code. Ghidra was used along with an MCP to reverse engineer the V.Flash’s hardware and how it works to reimplement in our SDK. The code that the AI wrote was in C and ARMv5 Assembly.

## Challenges we ran into

We ran into difficulties in terms of the emulator we used. The emulator we found for the V.Flash was EXTREMELY inaccurate in terms of graphics emulation and the AI had to figure out the accurate behavior by trial and error. I only managed to get a flat shaded (but GE enabled) version of Mario 64 before the deadline. If I had more time, I would had probably had gotten something closer to what I got on said "emulator".

## Accomplishments that we're proud of

We are proud of what we accomplished within the 24 hour time span. We were able to get a proof of concept version of Mario 64 up and running on real hardware with a GE backend, despite many technical difficulties. We were also able to uncover new information about the console.

## What we learned

We have learned so much about how the V.Flash works, how it's graphics engine worked, and how emulators being inaccurate can be problematic. We also learned about how early ARM compilers functioned and how VTech developed the console's architecture.

## What's next for V.Flash64

We hope to improve the Mario 64 proof of concept into an playable port. Including audio support, better remapping to the controller, optimization, improve graphics, etc. We are also going to polish up the SDK before public release on GitHub.

# Team Chocobo

## Inspiration

After the start time, the team set 1 hour to brainstorm as many ideas as possible. The timer was already long over when an idea suddenly came to the team's mind around one and a half hours in. The idea was a range slider to view significant historical events where users could select between 2 different years and see everything that happened in between.

The initial goal was to refine historical media into a selected range and display it.

We figured this would be a challenging project so we scoped in and asked ourselves, "what is something we all can relate to?". Well.. media and technology.

Our goal then became to give a user a simple high level dashboard of the most popular media and technology at that specific time. We wanted to refine the multiple search processes of "what movies were in 1997?" and "what games were popular in 1997?" into one interactive experience.

What Once Was was called What Was however "once" was added to make the acronym WOW.

## What it does

Users can explore years from 1995 to 2025 using an interactive timeline. Selecting a year updates the displayed content.

From here, users can see popular movies, music, video games, and technological improvements from that year.

Hovering over movie or game cards will give you fun facts about the media while the music player has a play button to allow the user to preview the song that topped that year's chart.

## How we built it

- Built using React and JavaScript with Tailwind CSS for styling.
- A local JSON dataset contains the cultural information of each year.
- The selected year determines which information is displayed.
- Integrated the Wikipedia/MediaWiki API to retrieve movie, game, and tech images.
- Integrated Apple iTunes Search API to retrieve music album art and audio.
- Used React components to separate the different content categories.

## Challenges we ran into

Working with external APIs was a bit challenging as reading through documentation while also juggling building proved to be a big blocker.

The first prototypes was sending almost 500 requests in just a single passthrough of the slider! (imagine going back and forth. one team member tested it and sent almost 5000 requests within 2 minutes..) The team implemented debouncing to prevent those requests from getting fetched and stale.

Deciding on which features to prioritize and keeping the project within scope and manageable within the time we had was one of the hardest parts as features could just be added left and right.

## Accomplishments that we're proud of

The team is particularly proud of the slider, design, and integrating several APIs.

We are also particularly proud of bringing several different cultural categories together into one application.

Lastly, the team is proud of completing a functional project at our first hackathon!

## What we learned

- The team gained experience working with external APIs and handling their responses.
- We learned more about React component structure, state management, and effects.
- We learned how to coordinate tasks and collaboration (as messy as it was) for our first "built from scratch" project.
- We learned the importance of balancing visual design, functionality, and development time.
- We gained experience turning ideas into one working application under a deadline.

## What's next for What Once Was

Beyond the hackathon, the project could expand the timeline to include years before 1995 or later on after 2025. There is also a lot of media we did not implement such as television, anime, books, and other forms of media.

The project could also expand by improving or introducing additional data sources and APIs.

The project is a static website and there is no website. Introducing a backend or database would make managing the expanding the timeline easier.

## AI use

AI was used to:

- generate static JSON data.
- debug source code.
- help team with planning components, pages, setup.
- act as a project manager.
- draft documentation framework for the repository `README`.
